technical_and_design_decisions: Use existing performance testing frameworks and scripts to measure and compare payload performance for baseline, Tuple, and Serialized types with specified sinks.

Modify Spring configuration properties to disable JMX by default, allowing for performance throughput benefits without manual intervention.
Debug and update Gradle build scripts to resolve issues with local ./gradlew dist and distZip targets, ensuring publish builds work correctly.
Systematically review and fix compiler and javadoc warnings to improve build output cleanliness and code maintainability.
Enhance RPM scripts to support starting multiple xd-container instances on the same node or VM, improving deployment flexibility.
Author user documentation for OOTB batch jobs and analytics tab widgets based on existing code, standards, and user needs.
assumptions: The developer has full access to the Spring XD codebase, development environment, and necessary tools (e.g., Java 17+, Gradle, testing frameworks).
Baseline performance data, test cases, or scripts for Kafka payload testing are available or can be derived from existing resources.
Documentation style guides, templates, and existing documentation are accessible to ensure consistency.
The upgrade to Reactor 2.0.3 is a minor version update that does not introduce breaking changes requiring significant refactoring.
Build issues are related to configuration or dependency problems that can be resolved without extensive architectural modifications.
RPM script modifications are feasible within the current deployment setup and do not require changes to core application logic.
Time estimates assume a standard workday and do not include external dependencies or delays beyond the developer's control.

Set up the test environment, rerun performance tests for the specified payloads and sinks on both Kafka versions, collect data, analyze results, and document performance differences.
Update Spring XD dependencies to Reactor 2.0.3, verify compatibility with existing code, build the project, and run regression tests to ensure no regressions or issues.
Modify Spring configuration files to set JMX disabled by default, update any related documentation or comments, and verify the change through testing.
Debug and resolve issues with local Gradle build targets (dist and distZip) to ensure publish builds work as expected, including testing build processes.
